terms.gloss: on time, at the right time
terms.comment: The adverb from tempus: “at the right or appointed time, in time” (Lewis & Short). Plautus’s and Cato’s word; it also serves for “in good time”.

evidence: Liv. 38.25 (ad tempus venīre, Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Also “for the time being” (Cic. Off. 1.27), so the context must make the sense clear.

terms.gloss: at the right moment, just in time
evidence: Ter. Heaut. 364: in tempore ad eam vēnī

phrases.latin: Numquid vīs? — Veniās temperī. — Memorem monēs.
phrases.english: “Anything else?” — “Mind you come on time.” — “No need to remind me.”

sources: Lewis & Short: tempus · Lewis & Short: temperi
Morgan–Owens, Adumbratio: s.v. time: on time.
